name: redwood2
note: The Redwood Coast pack rebuilt on Meshy (7 November 2026), the owner's request: the first pack, 5 November, drew fine sprays of needles; this one uses the tufted wording. Coast redwood, young redwood and tanoak; Douglas fir, western hemlock and western red cedar are the Pacific Northwest pack's. Form from the owner's Northwood photographs: very tall straight redwood trunks bare for half their height, crowns high, fog between them. Sizes PLACED. `seasons` are PLACED.
style: Stylised cartoon game art in soft, flat painted colour. Simple clean shapes with a gentle gradient: darker near the trunk and under each bough, lighter toward the tips. Matte, muted natural palette. No photographic detail, no photo bark, no noise, no speckle, no hard shadows, no highlights, no shine, no ink outlines, no text.
view: One view only, seen from the side at eye level, the whole plant in frame from foot to tip with a margin around it, centred, on a plain white background, in even soft light, with no cast shadow.

models.name: Blender_Redwood_1
models.colour: Foliage deep dull blue-green #2e4c40. Bark cinnamon red-brown #7a4a36.
models.prompt: A very tall old coast redwood tree beside a golf course, 55 m tall and 15 m wide, a tall narrow column. The tree stands upright and even, perfectly still on a calm day, nothing swept to one side, no lean. One straight slim trunk of cinnamon red-brown fibrous bark with shallow vertical flutes, completely bare for its lowest half. Above that long level boughs reaching well out from the trunk all the way to a narrow rounded top, the lower boughs reaching out a quarter of the tree's height on one side or the other. Each bough is a separate long soft tuft of foliage, thick and chunky with a lightly tufted scalloped edge, held out on its own visible bare limb, and the boughs grow singly at different heights on different sides of the trunk, some longer, some shorter, with the trunk and the limbs clearly seen between them and plenty of sky. An irregular, open, uneven outline. Never level rings or tiers around the trunk, no stacked layers, no skirts, no bowl, umbrella or saucer shapes, no repeating pattern. Paint the foliage as thick, solid three-dimensional forms, never as separate needles: no fine needles, no thin lines, no spiky bursts, no thin wisps, no hanging strands, nothing thinner than a limb. No solid core, no perfect spheres, no flat cone shape, no cones. A slim trunk, only one twenty-fourth of the tree's height wide near the ground, narrowing gently to two-thirds of that width at mid-height and to a narrow point at the top, its sides never parallel, slim compared with the wide boughs. Only a small flare in the very bottom of the trunk, no wide base. Whole healthy tree, no broken or snapped top. Stylised cartoon game asset, matte hand-painted colour. Single tree alone, no ground, no base, no text.
